scope: scripts/qualify_alarm_imports.py on a frozen Debug build of cb8a661 (D:\wp\b34), 82/82 steps, in one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with an SCL FB holding a Program_Alarm and its instance DB: plc_alarm_class_import (the project's alarm-class DAT with one edited display name), plc_alarm_instance_text_import (the instance-text workbook with one edited en-US alarm text), plc_supervision_import (the PLC's supervision workbook re-imported unchanged with Override; it initializes ProDiag's global settings, a recorded side effect) and plc_supervision_settings_import (the ProDiag settings DAT with one edited category display name), each applied with checkpoint, compile and save, asserted previews and change_status; every program export and member and plc_alarm_inspect's alarm classes, instance texts, supervisions and settings differ in exactly the intended keys and show the edit in a fresh export; a fresh owned Portal reopen shows the identical state; one import per kind restored from its checkpoint equals the reopened state. Typed refusals (ArtifactChanged, InvalidArtifact, InvalidRequest, PreviewMismatch, StaleRevision) change nothing.
limitations: Default alarm classes, one Program_Alarm instance and no ProDiag supervisions: plc_supervision_import re-imports an unchanged workbook; HMI consumers of the classes are not exercised.
plc_alarm_text_list_import is only refused: a scratch project has no user text list to export.
Engineering only; nothing is downloaded and no alarm is raised.
